title: BBAL: A Bidirectional Block Floating Point-Based Quantisation Accelerator for Large Language Models
problem: LLM deployment on edge devices faces memory and computational constraints; Block Floating Point (BFP) quantization loses small and moderate values because all data align to maximum exponent, degrading LLM accuracy.
motivation: Edge deployment of LLMs requires aggressive quantization; BFP promises lower overhead than FP but suffers quantization error from outlier-driven exponent alignment.
method: BBAL introduces Bidirectional Block Floating Point (BBFP) format that reduces selection of the maximum as shared exponent, lowering quantization error. Full-stack implementation includes BBFP processing element array and cost-effective nonlinear computation unit, enabling accurate low-bit LLM inference on edge accelerators.
key_novelty: Bidirectional exponent selection in BFP format reduces outlier-driven quantization error and enables practical hardware acceleration for LLMs.
contributions: Bidirectional Block Floating Point (BBFP) data format reducing quantization error
BBAL full-stack accelerator architecture with BBFP processing elements
Cost-effective nonlinear computation unit for low-precision arithmetic
22% accuracy improvement vs outlier-aware accelerators; 40% efficiency gain vs standard BFP
primary_theme: Bidirectional BFP quantization for low-precision LLM inference
